product.name: Rabbit R1
product.description: A small orange handheld with a screen, a camera, a scroll wheel, and a push-to-talk button. It is supposed to use your apps for you: order food, book a ride, and answer questions, without you opening those apps on a phone. No monthly fee.

brief.targetMarket: early adopters who want an AI assistant that takes actions, not just chat

actual.source: Preorders: first 10,000 units sold out in a day at CES, then a second 10,000 (The Verge, 2024-01-10). Ship date used as launch: late April 2024, with reviews on 2024-04-24. Units: CEO Jesse Lyu said 130,000 sold by Collision in June 2024 (Forbes, 2024-06-18). Usage: Lyu later said about 5,000 people were using a device at any time among roughly 100,000 buyers (The Verge, 2024-09-25). Reviews at ship called the device unfinished (The Verge, 'Nothing to see here', 2024-04-24). Addressable market of 500,000 is a stated assumption for early-adopter AI gadgets, not a company figure. Budget lines are not scored.
topComplaints: Could not reliably complete tasks in real apps
Felt like a phone app in a separate box
The action-model claim did not match what shipped
Little reason to carry it instead of a smartphone
actual.notes: Cumulative adoption is units sold divided by the 500,000 addressable market, so the sales spike is real: about 100,000 to 130,000 units in the first two months, then flat. That is not the same as retention. By September 2024 only about 5,000 people were using one at a time. The price of $199 was not the objection reviewers led with. A close prediction sells briskly at first and then stalls, and it names the 'why isn't this an app' objection before ship reviews existed.
